## Reconstruction-stage floors {#sec-ch08-reconfloors}

### Summary

A high-order reconstruction can overshoot into a negative face density or pressure even from a
perfectly admissible cell state. These floors catch that at the face, before the Riemann solver sees it.
The species faces are clamped at zero whenever the limiter is on, with or without `shock`, so a WENO undershoot cannot
carry vapour up a gradient; the density and pressure floors run only with `shock` false.
They belong to the reconstruction framework of @sec-ch04-framework and are described here because they
are part of the positivity story rather than part of the interpolation.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Clamp the reconstructed face states: density and pressure at the floors, tracers at zero.

**Data.** In: the left and right face states of one direction. Out: the same tensor clamped in place.

**Placement.** At the end of `ReconstructImpl::forward`, before the Riemann solver, every direction and stage.

**Activation.** `limiter: true`. Species: always. Density and pressure: only with `shock` false and the caller's `floor`.

**Guarantee / limits.** None: a clamp at the face invents mass, exactly as the cell floors of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter do.

**Evidence.** `[C2]`, `[C9]` of `floors_check`; `test_species_face_clamp.<b>` for the species faces under `shock`.
:::

### Derivation

None: a floor is a clamp, and everything said about non-conservation in @sec-ch08-eoslimiter applies
here too. Its check applies here too: `[C2]` measures the mass and energy a floor invents and finds
both strictly positive, because a clamp can only add [check `src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.py`,
output `src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.out`]. That is the shared property; the asymmetry below is
a branch structure, read from the code and not measured. What is worth recording is the asymmetry
between the three row groups, because it is not what a reader would guess.

Two early returns come first. A reconstruction with no hydro parent, the passive-scalar one
(@sec-ch08-scalar), clamps every row of its face states at zero, whatever the limiter, and returns (`phydro`,
{{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}). A reconstruction with `shock` set reconstructs every
row in one call, clamps the species rows at zero when the limiter is on, and returns before the density and pressure
floors (`shock`, {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}). The options start with `shock`
true (`shock`, {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.hpp ReconstructOptionsImpl >}}). The deck sets it false only through
`dynamics/reconstruct/vertical` for $x_1$ and `dynamics/reconstruct/horizontal` for $x_2$ and $x_3$
(`recon1`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}): `shock` is read, with false as its
default, only when that section exists. A deck without a `dynamics` or a `reconstruct`[^rg-345bdb73b555] block, or without the section
of a direction, keeps `shock` true there (`reconstruct`,
{{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}}; `section`,
{{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}), and that direction gets no
density or pressure face floors, even with the limiter on (`[C9]`). Its species faces are still clamped.

Past them, density and pressure are floored only when the caller asked for floors. Tracers are clamped at zero
whenever the limiter is on, *regardless* of what the caller asked, at
`clamp_min_` ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}). The well-balanced path of @sec-ch05 calls the reconstruction with
floors switched off precisely so that it can handle its own perturbation variables, and it still gets
its tracers clamped, with or without `shock`.

### Numerical method

With `shock` set, the species rows of the one-call result are clamped at `clamp_min_`
({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}) when the limiter is on and the state has species
rows. Every species row is clamped, clouds included, as on the non-shock path. With `shock` false the three groups are
floored in place as each is reconstructed: density at
`eos` ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}), pressure at `eos` ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}) and the tracers
at {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}. The values are read from the equation-of-state options and not
from the reconstruction options, which carry floor members that `forward` never reads.

**Why at the face, and what it costs.** Four facts of the code.

1. The floor values are read from the equation-of-state options and not from the reconstruction options, so the
   face and cell floors are the same absolute numbers ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}).
2. With a hydro parent, the tracer clamp is gated on the limiter alone, not on the caller's `floor` argument and not
   on `shock`, so the well-balanced path that passes `floor=false` still has its tracer face states clamped. With
   `shock` set density and pressure are not floored, and the passive-scalar reconstruction clamps every row with the
   limiter off too.
4. `clamp_min_` with a bound of zero leaves a face that is not negative as it was; the comment at the `shock` branch
   says so, and `test_species_face_clamp` checks that those faces are unchanged bit for bit
   ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}).
3. A clamp can only add; the mass it invents at a face is bounded by the overshoot it removes, and `[C2]` measures
   the cell-floor analogue strictly positive.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| the face density floor | {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}} | `density_floor` | limiter and floor |
| the face pressure floor | {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}} | `pressure_floor` | limiter and floor |
| the tracer clamp | {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}} | `clamp_min_` | limiter on, floor ignored |
| the tracer clamp under `shock` | {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}} | `shock` | limiter on, `shock` true |

: Code map of the reconstruction-stage floors. {#tbl-ch08-reconfloors-code}

**How to use it.** The face floors follow the limiter switch of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter; a caller opts out of the
density and pressure floors with the third argument of `forward`. The clamps are these lines
({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
  if (options->shock()) {
    _apply_inplace(dim, il, iu, w, pinterp1, result);
    ...
    if (phydro->options->eos()->limiter() && nvar > ICY) {
      result.narrow(1, ICY, nvar - ICY).clamp_min_(0.);
    }
    return result;
  }
  ...
  if (eos->limiter() && floor) {
    result.select(1, IDN).clamp_min_(eos->density_floor());
  }
  ...
  if (eos->limiter() && floor && result.size(1) > IPR) {
    result.select(1, IPR).clamp_min_(eos->pressure_floor());
  }
  ...
  if (eos->limiter()) {
    result.narrow(1, ICY, ny).clamp_min_(0.);
  }
```

`result` holds the left and right face states, `floor` is the caller's argument, and neither species clamp has a
`floor` test.

: Tests of the reconstruction-stage floors. {#tbl-ch08-reconfloors-tests}

The shared property is measured by `[C2]` of the chapter's check on the cell floors.[^ch08-reconfloors-run] `[C9]`:
without a `dynamics` or `reconstruct` block both directions keep `shock` true; with only a `vertical`[^rg-549637c96357] section $x_1$
has `shock` false and $x_2$, $x_3$ keep it true; with both sections both are false.

`test_species_face_clamp` reconstructs along $x_2$ a row of vapour mass fractions $10^{-16}$ with a slot of
$4.7\times10^{-3}$, $2.5\times10^{-9}$, $1.9\times10^{-5}$, by WENO5 with `scale` and `shock` on.[^ch08-reconfloors-ctest]
The smallest vapour face is $-2.2162\times10^{-5}$ with the limiter off and $0$ with it on, and the test's two
bitwise comparisons pass.

### Limits

1. **The tracer clamp ignores its caller.** A path that switches floors off to protect its own variables still has
   its tracer face states clamped, with or without `shock`. Whether that is intended is not recorded anywhere; the
   chapter records the behaviour.
2. **A clamp, not a limiter.** A species face raised to zero changes the face flux the tracer limiter of
   @sec-ch08-theta then scales, and so the mass it moves. The test checks the faces only; nothing in the repository
   measures the effect on a run's species budget.
3. **Same absolute values.** The face floors use the same absolute numbers as the cell floors, so the
   scaling caveat of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter applies to them unchanged.
